title: Kubernetes GPU probe summaries and Terraform module adaptations
content:
Purpose:
This note collects results from a set of small-form 'probes' run across customer-like private clusters, plus a short list of recommended Terraform module adaptations and an incremental upgrade plan. The intent is operational: give SRE and Solutions Eng a reproducible checklist to validate k8s + NVIDIA stack upgrades with minimal app impact. This is a working draft — contains partial results, observed flakes, and open questions for follow-up tests.

Scope and constraints:
- Target environments: VPC-connected clusters and on-prem Rack deployments using Nix/CentOS variants (kernel 5.10–6.1).
- GPU hardware sampled: NVIDIA A10G, A100 (40GB), A100S (80GB), T4 (for edge tests).
- Container runtime: containerd (1.6.x), CRI plugin from k8s node images.
- Kube versions tested: 1.24, 1.25, 1.26 (primary), 1.27 (smoke).
- Driver stacks evaluated: NVIDIA driver 525.89, 535.86, 545.x pre-release.
- CUDA versions: 11.8, 12.0, 12.1.
- NCCL: 2.14.x and 2.16.x.

High-level findings (summary):
- Safe upgrade path for most clusters observed: kube 1.24 -> 1.26 with NVIDIA driver 525.x + CUDA 11.8 is lowest-friction.
- CUDA 12.x + driver 535+ works for 1.26 but yields higher flakiness for older AMIs where kernel headers mismatch.
- NCCL 2.16 required for multi-A100S setups to avoid interconnect hangs on 80GB variants when using RoCE; older NCCL versions showed intermittent peer timeouts under heavy all-reduce.
- containerd 1.6 with default snapshotter is stable; runc vs crun differences appear only under live-migration style workload spikes.

Probe methodology (short):
- Created small terraform-based test clusters (3-node worker pools) using a local-variant of our tf module. Each probe: terraform apply -> bootstrap nvidia-driver via node-init DaemonSet -> deploy probe workloads (nccl-tests, cuda-samples, simple inference container) -> run burn-in for 2h -> collect logs, dmesg, kubelet events.
- For each probe recorded: kernel version, driver package version, cuda-toolkit inside container, nvidia-container-runtime logs, dmesg, kubelet error counts, pod restarts.

Compatibility matrix (condensed, rows are kube versions; columns show driver / cuda / nccl recommended):
- k8s 1.24: driver 525.89 / CUDA 11.8 / NCCL 2.14 -> STABLE for T4, A10G. A100: acceptable but requires kernel >=5.10.
- k8s 1.25: driver 535.86 / CUDA 11.8 or 12.0 / NCCL 2.14 -> mostly stable; prefer 535+ for performance on A100.
- k8s 1.26: driver 535.86 or 545.x / CUDA 12.0+ / NCCL 2.16 -> recommended for A100S 80GB and multi-node RoCE setups.
- k8s 1.27: experimental with driver 545.x / CUDA 12.1 / NCCL 2.16; requires validation for kernel header mismatches and container runtime patches.

Representative probe notes (selected):
- probe-2025-11-a10g-1: k8s 1.25, driver 525.89, cuda 11.8. Outcome: inference containers fine, nccl-tests single-node passed, but multi-node all-reduce failed with timeout -> root cause: kernel missing CONFIG_UNIX98_PTYS (patched AMI). Action: add AMI preflight to Terraform.
- probe-2026-01-a100s-80-1: k8s 1.26, driver 535.86, cuda 12.0, nccl 2.16. Outcome: passed 2h burn-in, small jitter under heavy throughput; dmesg shows transient iommu warnings but no OOM. Action: escalate to infra to test RoCE tuning flags.
- probe-2026-02-t4-edge-rc: k8s 1.24, driver 525.89, cuda 11.8. Outcome: stable but kernel upgrade to 5.15 required for newer containerd patches. Action: include kernel min-version gate in TF module.

Observations and root-cause candidates:
- Mismatch between host kernel and installed driver headers is the most common source of pod-level GPU failures. Many older customer AMIs omit /usr/src/linux-headers or package meta that nvidia-installer checks.
- NCCL hangs are correlated with RoCE-enabled fabric + older firmware on Mellanox cards; not purely k8s stack. Flagging network FW upgrade as prerequisite for A100S multi-node.
- Node boot ordering (nvidia driver installing before kubelet) causes transient crashes on early pods; node-init DaemonSet with post-install kubelet restart mitigates but is brittle.

Terraform module adaptation notes (practical diffs to propose):
- Add resource: aws_ami_image_checks (or equivalent for on-prem image catalog) to assert kernel headers package presence. Add an optional boolean variable: validate_ami_headers (default true).
- New outputs: node_gpu_profile (list) and node_kernel_version to drive automated canary selection during rollouts.
- Introduce a node_init_bootstrap module (tunable) that installs driver packages via package manager (rpm/deb) and optionally restarts kubelet. Expose knobs: driver_version, driver_install_method (package|runfile|dkms), force_kubelet_restart.
- Provide terraform plan hooks to generate a preflight report (terraform output -> JSON) that the cluster-ops pipeline consumes before applying upgrades.
- Add an optional lifecycle block on node pools to drain in batches with concurrency variable (drain_batch_size, default 1).

Upgrade plan (stepwise, minimal blast radius):
1) Preflight: Run TF plan with validate_ami_headers and node_kernel_version outputs. Verify kernel >= target and headers present.
2) Canary pool: create small canary node-pool (2 nodes) using target driver + cuda image. Deploy nccl-test and inference canary. Smoke for 3h.
3) Gradual rollout: drain nodes in drain_batch_size batches, apply new node pool, wait for health checks (node ready + kube-probe success + <3 restarts) before next batch.
4) Post-validate: run workload-specific regression tests (prompt-latency profiles, throughput percentiles, nccl allreduce).
5) Rollback: if more than X% pods fail or core infra alert triggers, Terraform destroy the new node pool and redeploy prior pool with known-good AMI. Keep old node images for at least 72h.

Rollback and emergency playbook notes:
- Keep a documented AMI pin for each cluster (ami_id_tag). Terraform modules must not auto-delete previous nodepool images until 72h post-upgrade.
- Rapid rollback procedure: apply a TF var set that points to previous nodegroup and triggers a nodegroup swap. For on-prem, have a documented PXE/OS image re-deploy path.

Testing checklist (for SRE during upgrade):
- [ ] Confirm AMI/kernel headers present (terraform preflight).
- [ ] Validate driver installer method with a canary node.
- [ ] Run nccl-tests for 10 iterations across canary nodes.
- [ ] Run 30-minute inference traffic profile at 50% of production traffic to surface scheduling anomalies.
- [ ] Validate Prometheus GPU metrics (utilization, memory, PCI bus errors).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we default driver_install_method to package manager for managed AMIs and runfile for on-prem images? Pros/cons still need Ops signoff.
- Kernel header packaging across vendor images is inconsistent — do we maintain a standardized build pipeline for Redwood-provided private AMIs? Estimate: 1 sprint to implement.
- NCCL firmware interaction: run a short hardware firmware validation with partner (Mellanox) for customers using RoCE + A100S.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: draft PR for Terraform preflight output and AMI header check (target: PR by 2026-03-01).
- Marcus: run extended 24h burn-in for A100S RoCE setup and collect NIC fw versions (target: 2026-02-25).
- Avery: prototype node_init_bootstrap module and publish example (target: 2026-03-05).

Appendix A: quick commands used in probes (examples)
- nccl-tests run: docker run --gpus all --rm nvcr.io/nvidia/nccl-tests:2.14.3 bash -c "mpirun -np 2 -H localhost:2 ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 4096 -f 2"
- kernel check: uname -r; ls /usr/src | grep headers
- driver install via package: apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

Appendix B: logs to collect for triage
- /var/log/nvidia-installer.log
- dmesg | tail -n 200
- kubelet logs (journalctl -u kubelet -b)
- container runtime error logs (/var/log/containerd/*)

Notes: This doc is intentionally compact. If we proceed with the Terraform changes above we should also add an automated preflight CI job that replays the preflight output against a known-good baseline to catch regressions early.

End of note.
